objectives: Describe how Stuxnet travelled from a USB stick to the program of a PLC
Map the main steps of Stuxnet to MITRE ATT&CK for ICS techniques
Explain why manipulating the operators' view made the physical damage possible
Relate Stuxnet's techniques to the PLC programming, Flood & Overwrite and MitM challenges on CybICS
takeaways: Stuxnet changed the program inside Siemens PLCs, not just the Windows computers around them.
It hid its changes from the engineers and replayed normal readings to the operators, so the plant looked healthy while centrifuges were damaged.
An air gap slowed the attack but did not stop it, because people carried data across it on USB sticks.
Knowing which program each PLC runs, and having an independent view of the process, are the defences that matter most.
Attribution to the United States and Israel is well-sourced reporting, never officially confirmed.

checkpoints.question: On CybICS you overwrite the HPT pressure value in register 1126. Which part of Stuxnet does this resemble most?
options: Crossing the air gap on infected USB sticks
Showing false process values to operators
Downloading new code blocks into the PLC
checkpoints.explanation: Overwriting the pressure value means the PLC and the FUXA HMI work with a number that is not the real pressure, just as Stuxnet's replayed values hid the real state of the centrifuges. It is tempting to call it a change of the PLC logic, but the program stays the same; only the value it reads is false. USB sticks were how Stuxnet got in, not what it did to the process.

quiz.question: Natanz was not connected to the internet. How did Stuxnet most likely get in?
options: Through an exposed Modbus port on the internet
On USB sticks carried in by people
Through a phishing e-mail to an operator
Through a vendor's remote-access VPN account
quiz.explanation: Stuxnet spread on USB sticks (T0847 Replication Through Removable Media) and then across the local network. Phishing and stolen remote-access accounts are common entry points in other incidents, such as the 2015 Ukraine attack and Colonial Pipeline, but an air-gapped plant offers neither; people carrying data in did.

quiz.question: Why did the engineers not see Stuxnet's code blocks when they looked at the PLC program in Step 7?
options: The blocks were encrypted, so Step 7 could not show them
A hooked Step 7 library hid them from the engineers
The malicious code ran on Windows, not inside the PLC
Signed drivers made Step 7 treat the blocks as genuine
quiz.explanation: Stuxnet replaced a Step 7 communication library (T0874 Hooking, T0851 Rootkit), so the engineering software showed a clean program. The blocks really were inside the PLC; the tool the engineers trusted lied about them. The stolen certificates only made Windows trust Stuxnet's drivers, they did not hide anything from Step 7.

quiz.question: Which ATT&CK for ICS techniques describe what Stuxnet did once it reached the PLC? (Select all that apply)
options: T0843 Program Download
T0836 Modify Parameter
T0832 Manipulation of View
T0847 Replication Through Removable Media
quiz.explanation: Stuxnet downloaded its own code to the PLC, changed the drive speed parameters and showed the operators false values. Replication Through Removable Media is real Stuxnet behaviour too, but it is how the worm got into the plant, before it ever reached a PLC.

quiz.question: On CybICS, which defence would most directly have caught a Stuxnet-style change to the OpenPLC program?
options: Comparing the running program with a known-good copy
Watching the FUXA HMI closely for unusual pressure readings
Moving the plant network behind an air gap
Encrypting the Modbus traffic between PLC and HMI
quiz.explanation: A program that differs from the approved copy is the clearest sign of tampering. Watching the HMI is the tempting answer, but Stuxnet's whole point was that the screens showed normal values. An air gap did not stop it at Natanz, and encryption protects traffic in transit, not a program uploaded by a trusted tool.

quiz.question: True or false: it is an officially confirmed fact that Stuxnet was built by the United States and Israel.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. The attribution rests on detailed press reporting, especially the New York Times in 2012, but no government has officially claimed Stuxnet. It is good practice to state that uncertainty.

attack.title: Put the attack in order
attack.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps of the Stuxnet attack into the order they happened, then give each one its MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactic.

steps.text: Infected USB sticks carried the worm into a plant with no internet connection.
steps.label: Initial Access
steps.explain: Nothing can happen before the worm is inside the plant. Replication Through Removable Media (T0847) is an Initial Access technique: it is how Stuxnet got its first foothold.

steps.text: Windows flaws, four of them unknown at the time, let the worm spread from computer to computer.
steps.label: Lateral Movement
steps.explain: Once inside, the worm had to find the computers that program the PLCs. Moving between hosts with Exploitation of Remote Services (T0866) is Lateral Movement.

steps.text: A replaced Step 7 library hid the malicious code blocks from the engineers looking at the PLC.
steps.label: Evasion
steps.explain: The swapped library had to sit on the engineering computer before any code reached a PLC, because Step 7 talks to the PLC through that library. Hiding from the defenders with Hooking and a Rootkit (T0874, T0851) is Evasion.

steps.text: The worm wrote its own code blocks into the Siemens PLCs.
steps.label: Persistence
steps.explain: With the cover in place, the code went into the controllers (T0843 Program Download). Modify Program (T0889) is a Persistence technique: the malicious blocks stay in the PLC and run on every cycle.

steps.text: The PLCs ordered the centrifuge drives to speeds far above and far below normal.
steps.label: Impair Process Control
steps.explain: Only the code inside the PLC could command the drives. Changing setpoints with Modify Parameter (T0836) and Manipulation of Control (T0831) is Impair Process Control.

steps.text: Iran removed a large number of centrifuges at Natanz, which most researchers link to the worm.
steps.label: Impact
steps.explain: The removals came after months of stressful speed changes. Damaged machines are the physical result the attack aimed at, and that result is the Impact tactic.
